Full withdrawal of labour.provides: complete cessation of cargo handling, a known end date in most cases

Work to rule.provides: throughput reduced by a third, no legal exposure for the workforce

Refusal to handle specific cargo.provides: selective disruption, other trade continuing normally

Automation dispute over new equipment.provides: disruption concentrated at one terminal, a structural rather than a pay issue

Single dominant national port.requires: most national trade through one estuary
Single dominant national port.provides: no domestic alternative, immediate national effect

Several competing terminals.requires: rival operators in the same range
Several competing terminals.provides: diversion possible between terminals, competitive pressure on the operator

Landlord port with many operators.requires: an authority leasing to independent stevedores
Landlord port with many operators.provides: dispute confined to one employer, others unaffected

Fully automated terminal.provides: very few workers to withdraw, a small technical workforce with high leverage

Divert to another port.provides: continuity at higher cost, inland transport rebalanced

Use of contractor labour.requires: workers willing to cross and legal permission
Use of contractor labour.provides: partial throughput, severe escalation of the dispute

Arbitration and settlement.provides: resolution rather than substitution, days to weeks

Emergency legal powers.provides: forced resumption, political and legal challenge

Shortage of specific goods.provides: empty shelves in some categories only

Manufacturing stoppage.provides: production halted, cost far exceeding the freight value

DISPUTE FORM|PORT CHARACTERISTIC.requires: an authority leasing to independent stevedores

DISPUTE FORM|MITIGATION.requires: workers willing to cross and legal permission
